//: GitLab uses its own header rather than Authorization.
//endpoints: GitLab addresses a project by a URL-encoded owner/name pair rather than a path, so {owner} and {repo} are separated by %2F here rather than a slash.
//repositoryFields: Note how little of this matches Gitea: different field names, a nested owner path, and a visibility string instead of a boolean.
//gitCredentials: GitLab wants a fixed username with the token as the password.
//pullRequestFields: A merge request is a pull request under another name. Note iid, not id: the per-project number is what appears in the URL and in the ref, while id is global and would name someone else's merge request entirely.
//pullRequestRef: GitLab files merge request heads somewhere else entirely, which is why this is a manifest field and not a constant.
//webUrls: The one place GitLab's website differs in shape from everyone else's: a /-/ between the project and the page. Opening a merge request is a form with its own query parameters rather than a compare page.
